main_text.p: Ξυσὸς, inter alia, genus vestis interioris: χιλὰν ξυσὸς, & ξυσὸς χιλωνικὸν: & simpliciter, ξυσαί, interula, ex scissura vel incisura sic dicta: a shirt.

Ξάγαεις vel σίγγαεις, gladius Persicus, secutis: σίγαεις λυσφλεβὶς, scalprum chirurgicum (ut Celsus appellat:) quo venæ aperiuntur. Vox origine Scythica, sed Græcis satis familiaris. Cujus vestigia in Saxon. verbo {bl}fearen{/bl}; de quo verbo plura dicemus in postremâ parte.
Ξλίχω, columna, cui ædificium aliudve innititur; a stoole.
Ξληεα, sterilis, βῶς ςιῆα, apud Homerum, vacca. Anglis, a steere, juvencus: ob castrationem sterilis scil. & tauro oppositus.

Ξτίρχα, σπέρχω, urgeo, festino, &c. σπερχυὸς, festinans, pernix, studiosus, studiosè incumbens alicui rei. Nescio an hinc sparth, de infignioris agilitatis & alacritatis puero; an potius metaphora sit à sparth, scintilla. Sed est præterea σπερχυὸς, ξίΘ (ut Hesychius) ξεγκ, genus accipitris. Angl. a sparhawke, vel sparrow-hawke: ex Græco fine dubio; nisi hoc ipsum verbum Anglicum

page.notes: Greek words are transcribed approximately; the Greek type is heavily worn and several accents and letters are doubtful. Old English words (steere, stoole, shirt, fearen, sparhawke) may be imperfect. Catchword "Anglicum" at the foot right is printed as the last word of the page.
